contentFull:
Poultry India Expo 2026 to bring global industry to Hyderabad

The 18th edition of Poultry India Expo will take place from 25-27 November 2026 at the Hitex Exhibition Centre in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. The event will bring together poultry professionals from across the value chain, with a focus on technology, biosecurity, sustainable nutrition and automation.

Sep 3

Partner

The Poultry Knowledge Day seminar will precede the exhibition on 24 November at HICC/Novotel, Hitech City, Hyderabad.

Connecting India's poultry industry

The event is organised by the Indian Poultry Equipment Manufacturers’ Association (IPEMA), which represents manufacturers of poultry equipment in India. The association promotes innovation, standardisation and sustainable practices across the poultry value chain and supports the adoption of smart farming technologies, animal health solutions and domestic agri-tech developments.

Poultry India Expo is IPEMA’s flagship event and has expanded steadily in both scale and international participation.

More than 51,000 visitors in 2025

The 17th edition in 2025 attracted more than 500 exhibitors from over 50 countries and recorded 51,251 industry visitors. The exhibition covered approximately 35,000 square metres across 7 air-conditioned halls.

Live demonstrations and displays covered breeding and genetics, hatchery and farm automation, feed milling, housing and ventilation, veterinary diagnostics, biosecurity, egg processing and manure management.

The accompanying Knowledge Day addressed topics including emerging diseases, feed planning, sustainability, rural market opportunities and career development in the poultry sector.

India’s growing poultry sector

India is the world’s second-largest egg producer, with output reaching 142.77 billion eggs in 2023-24. The country is also among the world’s top 4 broiler-producing countries.

Poultry plays an important role in India’s nutrition security and rural employment. According to the organisers, annual growth of chicken meat production has remained at around 8-10%, while egg production has grown by 6-8% in recent years.

The sector is continuing to modernise, creating demand for technologies that can improve productivity, efficiency, animal health and sustainability.

Focus areas for 2026

The 2026 exhibition will focus on biosecurity, sustainable nutrition, automation and the competitiveness of the Indian poultry sector.

Organisers expect more than 550 exhibitors and over 51,000 industry professionals from more than 80 countries. Key areas will include:

Networking and knowledge exchange across the poultry value chain

New technologies in breeding, hatchery systems, feed milling and farm automation

Advances in veterinary products, poultry housing, egg processing and manure management

Business development and partnership opportunities

Knowledge Day

The Knowledge Day on 24 November will feature international and Indian speakers discussing current challenges and future opportunities for the poultry sector.

The programme will build on themes addressed in 2025, including disease prevention, feed strategies, sustainability and developing the next generation of industry talent.

International participation

Poultry India Expo has established links with more than 20 overseas poultry associations and over 40 national poultry bodies.

The Hitex Exhibition Centre offers more than 35,000 square metres of exhibition space across 7 modern, air-conditioned halls. Exhibition hours will be from 10:00 to 18:00 each day.

The organisers are inviting poultry farmers, breeders, integrators, equipment manufacturers, researchers, veterinarians, policymakers, students and young professionals to attend.

With the Knowledge Day on 24 November followed by 3 days of exhibition activity, Poultry India Expo 2026 aims to provide a platform for technical knowledge exchange, networking and business development across the poultry sector.

Further information is available from IPEMA at info@poultryindia.co.in or via the Poultry India website.
translationZh:
第18届印度家禽博览会将于2026年11月25日至27日在印度特伦甘纳邦海得拉巴的Hitex展览中心举行。该活动将汇聚家禽价值链各环节的专业人士，重点关注技术、生物安全、可持续营养和自动化。

家禽知识日研讨会将于11月24日在海得拉巴Hitech City的HICC/诺富特酒店举行，作为博览会的会前活动。

**连接印度家禽产业**

该活动由印度家禽设备制造商协会（IPEMA）主办，该协会代表印度家禽设备制造商。协会在家禽价值链中推动创新、标准化和可持续实践，并支持智能养殖技术、动物健康解决方案和国内农业科技发展的应用。

印度家禽博览会是IPEMA的旗舰活动，在规模和国际参与度上持续稳步扩大。

**2025年观众超过5.1万人**

2025年的第17届博览会吸引了来自50多个国家的500多家展商，录得51,251名行业观众。展览面积约35,000平方米，分布在7个空调展厅内。

现场演示和展示涵盖育种与遗传学、孵化场和农场自动化、饲料加工、房舍与通风、兽医诊断、生物安全、蛋品加工和粪污管理。

同期举办的知识日讨论了新兴疾病、饲料规划、可持续性、农村市场机会和家禽行业职业发展等主题。

**印度家禽业持续增长**

印度是世界第二大鸡蛋生产国，2023-24年度产量达到1427.7亿枚。该国也是全球前四大肉鸡生产国之一。

家禽业在印度的营养安全和农村就业中发挥着重要作用。据主办方介绍，近年来鸡肉产量年增长率保持在8-10%左右，鸡蛋产量年增长率为6-8%。

该行业持续现代化，对能够提高生产力、效率、动物健康和可持续性的技术产生了需求。

**2026年重点领域**

2026年博览会将重点关注生物安全、可持续营养、自动化以及印度家禽业的竞争力。

主办方预计将有来自80多个国家的550多家展商和超过5.1万名行业专业人士参加。关键领域包括：

- 家禽价值链的交流与知识分享
- 育种、孵化系统、饲料加工和农场自动化领域的新技术
- 兽药产品、家禽房舍、蛋品加工和粪污管理的进展
- 业务发展和合作伙伴机会

**知识日**

11月24日的知识日将邀请国际和印度演讲者讨论家禽行业当前面临的挑战和未来机遇。

该议程将延续2025年的主题，包括疾病预防、饲料策略、可持续性以及培养下一代行业人才。

**国际参与**

印度家禽博览会已与20多个海外家禽协会和40多个国内家禽组织建立了联系。

Hitex展览中心提供超过35,000平方米的展览空间，分布在7个现代化空调展厅内。展览开放时间为每天10:00至18:00。

主办方邀请家禽养殖户、育种者、一体化企业、设备制造商、研究人员、兽医、政策制定者、学生和年轻专业人士参加。

随着11月24日的知识日及随后3天的展览活动，2026年印度家禽博览会旨在为家禽行业的技术知识交流、社交和业务发展提供一个平台。

更多信息可通过info@poultryindia.co.in联系IPEMA，或访问Poultry India网站获取。
author: India Poultry Equipment Manufacturers Association
